Definition: of Chaldee origin (compare H6646); the gazelle; Tabitha (i.e. Tabjetha), a Christian female:--Tabitha.
BiblicalUsage: Tabitha, also called Dorcas, was a disciple at Joppa full of good works and almsdeeds, and the widows showed Peter the coats she had made. When she died, Peter was sent for; he put them all out, knelt down, and said, Tabitha, arise. The name means gazelle, and Luke tells the story as plainly as he can: she died, Peter prayed, and she opened her eyes.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Tabitha's story is about the kind of life that leaves coats behind it. I hold that quiet good works are never wasted, and that the God who raised her notices every one of them.
